title: Keeping solutions at the right temperature
body: In a school chemistry laboratory, the teacher keeps two solutions in separate water baths. A dilute hydrochloric acid solution must be kept at a temperature strictly between 30 degrees Celsius and 35 degrees Celsius. A second solution must be kept strictly between 68 degrees Fahrenheit and 77 degrees Fahrenheit. The thermometer on the first bath reads in degrees Fahrenheit, while the one on the second bath reads in degrees Celsius, so the students must convert the ranges. They use the conversion formula C = (5/9)(F - 32), or equivalently F = (9/5)C + 32, where C and F are the temperatures in degrees Celsius and degrees Fahrenheit.
